newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO negotiators see U.S. envoy in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: PLO negotiators see U.S. envoy in Jerusalem.

text.p: The chief Palestinian peace negotiators met a U.S. presidential envoy on Friday in a bid to save Israel-PLO peace talks in crisis over Jewish settlement and violence.

Saeb Erekat and Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, were meeting the envoy Dennis Ross at a Jerusalem hotel ahead of Ross's meeting later in the day with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Ross met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Morocco and then flew to Israel where he met Netanyahu late on Thursday. U.S. President Bill Clinton said the Ross-Arafat talks were encouraging but did not elaborate.

Erekat said before meeting Ross the only way out of the crisis -- marked by eight days of clashes and an Islamist suicide bombing that killed three Israelis a week ago -- was for Israel to stop work on a Jewish settlement on a hilltop in Arab East Jerusalem.
"There is one item on the agenda: the current state of the peace process," Erekat told Reuters. "If Netanyahu orders the bulldozers to stop I think the peace process will be on track."
"Settlement and peace don't go together just as violence and peace don't go together."

Asked whether Arafat's Palestinian Authority accepted Israel's demand it crack down on militants, Erekat said: "This has been our position, but we don't follow such demands by media lords like Netanyahu."
Erekat blamed Netanyahu for the escalation in violence, saying: "I urge him to come back to sanity and courage."
